text: Dawn broke over Foni Bondali in hues of violet and gold.
The wedding drums began their thunderous beat, and guests arrived from every village along the river.
But inside his bedchamber, Massaneh did not rise.
When his brothers entered to drape him in his wedding damask, they found him still and cold, claimed peacefully in his sleep before the first ray touched his face.

The wedding turned to weeping, the bride returned to her home, and by sunset the jali began the song that would echo across Senegambia forever: Massaneh Ceesay had all the gold of the earth, but not a single second to spend it.
